profile.reading:
The building identified at this location on New Albany Road East in New Albany, a planned community in Franklin County just northeast of Columbus, Ohio, is associated with TJX Companies, the Framingham, Massachusetts based off price retailer that operates T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Sierra, and related chains across North America and Europe. TJX does not publish a facility level description, address confirmation, square footage, or power capacity for a technology building at this location, and no corporate press material ties a specific building to this address beyond what is captured in mapping data, so this profile is built primarily on locality and industry context rather than a confirmed specification sheet.

New Albany itself is informative context. Originally developed as a corporate campus community starting in the 1990s, the village became home to the headquarters or major campuses of companies including L Brands and Bath and Body Works, Abercrombie and Fitch, Discover Financial Services, and American Electric Power, and over the past decade the surrounding New Albany International Business Park has become one of the largest concentrations of hyperscale data center construction in the Midwest, with facilities built by Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft drawn by American Electric Power's transmission infrastructure and by state and local tax incentives for data center development. A large national retailer siting a technology facility in this corridor would fit an established pattern: companies headquartered on the East Coast frequently place backup or secondary data processing infrastructure in the Midwest for geographic redundancy, and Ohio in particular has built a reputation as a lower cost, lower risk location for that kind of build out relative to coastal markets.

TJX has a particular reason to take data infrastructure seriously that is a matter of public record. The company disclosed in 2007 that intruders had accessed its payment systems and stolen tens of millions of customer payment card records over a period of years, one of the largest retail data breaches publicly documented at the time, and the incident is widely understood to have pushed the company toward significant, sustained investment in its information technology and network security posture afterward. Beyond that broader context, however, no permit record, square footage figure, or capacity figure specific to this New Albany Road East address is publicly available, and this profile does not estimate one.
